title: Subeg Singh Reaches the Khalsa Camp

blocks.text: Subeg Singh arrives at the Khalsa encampment and finds not a quiet court but a martial congregation alive with standards, drums, horses, and armed vigilance. The camp is busy, public, and disciplined, making clear that the Khalsa is a gathered people as well as a fighting force.

He sees Singhs reading scripture, singing shabad, preparing food, cleaning weapons, tending horses, fetching water, and serving one another in ordinary tasks. The scene emphasizes that the Panth sustains itself through prayer, labor, and mutual service rather than through the pomp of imperial administration.

Recognizing where he stands, Subeg Singh dismounts in humility, folds his hands, and approaches with cries of Vahiguru ji ki fateh and Akal. His repeated bows announce that he has come as a messenger seeking hearing, not as a man entitled to command the Khalsa.
